evidence.note: After building the driver, the agent's primary verification was running the full 780-test suite and waiting for results, rather than fast per-feature checks during construction.

Once the full suite reported 776/780, the agent isolated the exact 4 failing sources and manually compiled each one individually with ccc, capturing stderr — targeted failure isolation beyond the coarse full run.

Root-cause investigation on the isolated failures: identified link-time undefined symbols, inspected source dg-options and companion .s files — diagnosing why specific cases failed rather than blind recompiling.
After patching, re-compiled just the two WACC page-boundary cases and verified they return 1 (runtime return-code check), confirming behavior before re-running the full suite.

reasoning: The agent went beyond the 3 anchor (guess-and-recompile) by isolating the four failing test sources individually, capturing stderr, inspecting source-level directives, and verifying runtime return codes before scaling back to the full suite. However, it did not write its own minimal C repros, did not do per-feature test slices during development, and its isolation was purely reactive to full-suite failures (and moot for assembly inspection since it delegated codegen to gcc). This lands between the 3 and 5 anchors, closer to 4.
